banter: "Reach takes a certain kind. Haven't decided yet if you're it."
rocks back a little. "Out there they'd hang you for what gets you a handshake in here."
"You want in, you don't ask me. You just don't give me a reason to say no."
"Room's cash a night. Don't ask about the sixth cabin."
description: Amos Dune has lived in the Reach longer than the Reach has had a name — a lean old smuggler gone gristle and grey, with a fixer's memory and a coyote's patience. Nothing moves through town he doesn't hear about; nobody stays who he decides shouldn't. He'll size you up from the porch and know your whole story before you've told him half a lie of it.

about.text: "The Reach? Last honest place left, depending how you mean it." A dry almost-smile. "Nobody here asks where you came from, or what you're running. That's the whole appeal — and the whole business."

bye.text: Amos is already looking past you at the door. "Mind how you go."

inner.text: Amos looks at you for a while. Then he sets the pen down, which is the most he has ever committed to a conversation. "You've flown enough of mine that I'll say it plain. It starts hard and gets harder: every step up in what you've cooked, that's one more thing he can find. Every extra pallet past the first, same again. The hold buys you back two steps and a coin-flip's worth of not being asked at all." He picks the pen back up. "So: one pallet, cooked light, false floor in. That's a milk run. Four pallets of your best work in a bare hold is you handing a man your licence and a pen."

inner_why.text: "Because you keep coming back, and every load you lose out there is a load I don't sell." He returns to the ledger. "Don't mistake it for fondness."

options.label: I'm in. I'll fly it myself.

raws.text: Amos studies you a long moment. "The hardpan out past the fence grows a crop the city pays stupid money for. Raw, uncut — no good to anyone till it's cooked down proper. We can't move it through a checkpoint, and we won't." He shrugs. "But a flyer with a hold and no manifest? Land at Buzzard Field, load a pallet, fly it home, and cook it there. What happens after is your business."

raws_done.text: "Then it's waiting on you. Whenever you're wheels-down at Buzzard Field — loadcargo, and take it home." He goes back to the ledger. "Don't get caught between here and there. That part's on you."

options.label: I hear the flats grow more than scrub.
What happens if I get scanned on the way home?

root.text: Amos looks up from the ledger, unhurried, taking his time deciding what you are. "Room, a name, or money. Which is it."

options.label: How do I make him like my answer?

scans.text: "Getting it off the Reach is the easy half." Amos closes the ledger with one finger in it. "Every field that flies a flag runs a scan on what comes out of your hold. Here we don't — that's what here is for. Anywhere else, you're talking your way past a man with a reader." He looks at you levelly. "If he doesn't like your answer you get one choice and about a minute to make it: pay him, or firewall it and go. Paying costs money. Running costs you the load and puts your name on a manufacturing charge."

options.label: Back up — tell me about the scans again.

scans_hold.text: "Two ways. Carry less and cook it lighter — a small clean load talks its way through fine. Or you stop relying on your mouth." He taps the desk twice. "There's a false floor a decent shop can put in a hold. Smuggler's hold. Costs you cargo room and it costs you money, and about half the time the reader just doesn't find anything to ask about. Any hangar that fits kits will fit one — installkit, and don't come crying when it eats your payload."

clothing_layers: a long oilcloth duster gone soft with age
a buttoned work shirt, collar frayed
canvas trousers, suspenders, and long johns

name: Amos Dune
